content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], can you assist me in checking my [product_name] program and [product_name] project? I'm experiencing the same issue as with AutoGen_7366596 while using [product_name] [version_no]. I've attached a zip file for your review and support. Thanks in advance.
You don't have any overlaps in your configuration. However, I recommend using the "Scale Time" component with the timers instead of "Analog Value".
Hi [user_name], sorry for originally sending an outdated [product_name] file. Please check the attached latest version I am currently using. I'm unable to modify the yearly timer figure. Thanks.
Hello [user_name], I am sending another attachment with additional details for your information. Thanks.

Since I'm unclear on your exact requirements, could you share what parameters you entered in the VM mapping table for the yearly timer? Are you aiming to alter the on-year and off-time via the web server? With the current setup, you do have overlapping entries.

I'd like to change the date (year-month-day) using the web server. For instance, if today is Dec 27th, 2023, I would set the AC to run from Dec 28th, 2023 to Dec 30th, 2023. There are two cells: the upper one turns on the AC starting Dec 28th, and the lower one turns it off on Dec 30th. However, I'm unable to input or modify these dates through the web server or [product_name] software. Please see the attachment for reference. I'm unsure what needs correction. Thank you.

You previously uploaded a different program than the one you're now showing in your screenshot. It appears you've uploaded the prior version. Your working method seems a bit disorganized, especially regarding data backup.

Hello [user_name], apologies for the confusion. I didn't update you with the most recent changes made during our discussion, as I was trying to pinpoint the issue, which led to some alterations I forgot to share. Please find the newest version attached. I still haven't identified the fault yet. Thanks for your patience.
There are overlapping entries in your configuration. Refer to the corrected Parameter VM Mapping table.
Thank you so much, [user_name]. I have resolved the issue based on your suggested corrections.

Good morning, [user_name]. I added a year field according to the image, but is there a way to display the year as 2023, 2024, etc., instead of the current view? I am also attaching my [product_name] files for your review if needed. Thank you.

Please modify the Parameter VM Mapping table entries as shown in the attached screenshot. Change the input/output fields in [product_name] from scale time to analog value, and set the block format to Hex.

Hi [user_name], please help correct my [product_name] files. They still aren't functioning as intended, as seen in the image below. I've followed your advice, but the system displays 2400 instead of 2024. Attachment included for your review. Thank you.
No, the corrections I suggested were not applied. In your [product_name] program, the Parameter VM Mapping table remains uncorrected, as seen in the previous screenshot.

Hi [user_name], I applied your suggested changes (VM is 13,…71), but the timer still doesn't run correctly and I'm unable to update the figures (it seems like an overlap issue), so I reverted to the previous address for these four fields. For your information. Thank you.

I tested it with the suggested settings and it worked as expected, but only for the first entry (VW12). VW12 consists of VB12 and VB13. If you change the mapping from VB12 to VB13, then the year appears in VB13. When accessing the web server initially, it shows 0024 (00 is VB12, 24 is VB13). Entering 2024 in the web server's input field updates VB12 to 20 and VB13 to 24, resulting in VW12 displaying 2024.
Good morning [user_name], understood! After making the changes you suggested, everything works as I wanted. You are truly knowledgeable in this area. Thank you very much, [user_name].
